model.name: Plant Disease Detection Model V2
model.description: EfficientNetV2B0-based plant disease detection trained on PlantVillage dataset

classes.name: Bell Pepper - Bacterial Spot
symptoms: Small, water-soaked spots on leaves and fruit
Spots turn brown with yellow halos
Lesions may coalesce causing blighted areas
Premature fruit drop in severe cases
classes.causes: Caused by Xanthomonas campestris pv. vesicatoria, spread by rain splash, wind, and infected seeds

treatment.chemical: Apply copper-based bactericides (copper hydroxide or copper sulfate) at 7-10 day intervals
treatment.cultural: Remove and destroy infected plant material, avoid overhead irrigation, improve air circulation
treatment.preventive: Use certified disease-free seeds, practice 2-3 year crop rotation, avoid working in wet fields

classes.urgency: Medium - treat within 1 week to prevent spread
classes.economic_impact: Can reduce yield by 20-50% under severe epidemic conditions

classes.name: Bell Pepper - Healthy
symptoms: Bright green, firm leaves with no discoloration
Normal leaf shape and texture
Vigorous plant growth with no lesions
classes.causes: No disease present - plant is in good health

treatment.cultural: Continue regular watering, fertilization, and monitoring
treatment.preventive: Maintain proper spacing, avoid overwatering, scout regularly for early disease detection

classes.urgency: None - plant is healthy, continue routine care
classes.economic_impact: No negative impact - healthy plants produce optimal yield

classes.name: Potato - Early Blight
symptoms: Dark brown to black lesions with concentric rings (target-board pattern)
Lesions surrounded by yellow chlorotic tissue
Lower leaves affected first, progressing upward
Premature defoliation in severe cases
classes.causes: Caused by Alternaria solani fungus; favored by warm temperatures (24-29°C) and high humidity

treatment.chemical: Apply chlorothalonil, mancozeb, or copper-based fungicides every 7-10 days
treatment.cultural: Remove infected lower leaves, avoid overhead watering, improve plant spacing for airflow
treatment.preventive: Plant certified disease-free tubers, practice 3-4 year crop rotation, maintain adequate soil fertility

classes.urgency: Medium - treat within 1-2 weeks before significant defoliation occurs
classes.economic_impact: Can reduce tuber yield by 20-30% and reduce tuber quality if severe

classes.name: Potato - Late Blight
symptoms: Water-soaked, pale green lesions on leaves that rapidly turn brown-black
White fluffy sporulation visible on underside of leaves in humid conditions
Brown lesions on stems, often causing collapse
Infected tubers show reddish-brown dry rot internally
classes.causes: Caused by Phytophthora infestans oomycete; spreads rapidly in cool, moist weather (10-20°C)

treatment.chemical: Apply systemic fungicides (metalaxyl, cymoxanil) or protectants (chlorothalonil, mancozeb) preventively every 5-7 days
treatment.cultural: Remove and destroy all infected plant material immediately, avoid overhead irrigation, hill soil to protect tubers
treatment.preventive: Plant resistant varieties, use certified seed potatoes, apply preventive fungicides during cool/wet periods

classes.urgency: High - immediate action required, disease can destroy entire crop within days
classes.economic_impact: Historically devastating - can cause 100% crop loss under epidemic conditions; caused the Irish Famine

classes.name: Potato - Healthy
symptoms: Dark green, robust foliage with no lesions
Normal leaf texture and color
Vigorous stem growth with no signs of infection
classes.causes: No disease present - plant is in good health

treatment.cultural: Continue regular hilling, watering, and monitoring
treatment.preventive: Scout regularly, maintain proper irrigation, consider preventive fungicide program during rainy periods

classes.urgency: None - plant is healthy, continue routine care
classes.economic_impact: No negative impact - healthy plants produce optimal tuber yield

classes.name: Tomato - Bacterial Spot
symptoms: Small, water-soaked spots on leaves, stems, and fruit
Spots turn brown-black with yellow halos on leaves
Scabby, raised lesions on fruit surface
Defoliation in severe infections
classes.causes: Caused by Xanthomonas vesicatoria; spreads via rain splash, wind, and contaminated tools

treatment.chemical: Apply copper-based bactericides with mancozeb every 5-7 days during wet weather
treatment.cultural: Stake plants for better air circulation, remove infected leaves, avoid working when plants are wet
treatment.preventive: Use disease-free transplants and seeds, practice crop rotation, avoid overhead irrigation

classes.urgency: Medium - treat within 1 week, especially before rainy periods
classes.economic_impact: Can reduce marketable fruit yield by 10-40%; fruit blemishes reduce market value significantly

classes.name: Tomato - Early Blight
symptoms: Dark brown lesions with concentric rings on lower leaves
Yellow chlorosis surrounding lesions
Lesions may coalesce, causing large necrotic areas
Stem lesions (collar rot) can cause plant death in young transplants
classes.causes: Caused by Alternaria solani fungus; favored by alternating wet and dry conditions with warm temperatures

treatment.chemical: Apply chlorothalonil, azoxystrobin, or copper fungicides at first sign of disease, repeat every 7-10 days
treatment.cultural: Remove and compost infected lower leaves, mulch to prevent soil splash, stake plants
treatment.preventive: Plant resistant varieties, avoid excessive nitrogen fertilization, maintain proper plant spacing

classes.urgency: Medium - treat within 1-2 weeks to prevent defoliation
classes.economic_impact: Causes 20-40% yield reduction; defoliation reduces fruit quality and sun-scalds fruit

classes.name: Tomato - Late Blight
symptoms: Pale green to brown water-soaked patches on leaves
White mold growth on underside of affected leaves
Brown, greasy-looking lesions on stems
Brown to dark brown firm rot on fruit
classes.causes: Caused by Phytophthora infestans; thrives in cool (10-20°C), wet conditions with high humidity

treatment.chemical: Apply systemic fungicides (cymoxanil, famoxadone) immediately; preventive copper sprays during cool/wet weather
treatment.cultural: Remove and bag all infected material, never compost infected plants, improve field drainage
treatment.preventive: Plant resistant varieties, apply preventive fungicides during cool/wet forecasts, avoid dense planting

classes.urgency: High - immediate treatment required; can destroy entire crop within 7-10 days
classes.economic_impact: Can cause 70-100% crop loss in epidemic years; one of the most destructive tomato diseases

classes.name: Tomato - Leaf Mold
symptoms: Pale green to yellow spots on upper leaf surface
Olive-green to grayish-brown velvety mold on underside of leaves
Leaves eventually turn yellow and drop
Primarily affects lower canopy leaves first
classes.causes: Caused by Fulvia fulva (Passalora fulva) fungus; favored by high humidity (>85%) and poor air circulation

treatment.chemical: Apply chlorothalonil, mancozeb, or copper fungicides; copper-based fungicides work well
treatment.cultural: Increase ventilation in greenhouses, reduce humidity by improving spacing and pruning
treatment.preventive: Use resistant varieties, prune suckers for better air circulation, avoid overhead irrigation

classes.urgency: Medium - treat within 1-2 weeks, particularly important in greenhouse settings
classes.economic_impact: Can reduce yield by 20-30%; primarily a problem in greenhouse production

classes.name: Tomato - Septoria Leaf Spot
symptoms: Numerous small, circular spots with dark brown borders and lighter gray centers
Tiny black fruiting bodies (pycnidia) visible in spot centers
Lower leaves affected first, progressing upward
Severe defoliation leaving fruit exposed to sunscald
classes.causes: Caused by Septoria lycopersici fungus; spreads via water splash, favored by warm (20-25°C) wet conditions

treatment.chemical: Apply chlorothalonil, mancozeb, or copper-based fungicides every 7-10 days
treatment.cultural: Remove and destroy infected leaves, mulch soil to prevent splash dispersal, stake plants
treatment.preventive: Rotate crops for 3+ years, use disease-free transplants, avoid overhead irrigation

classes.urgency: Medium - treat promptly to prevent extensive defoliation and fruit quality loss
classes.economic_impact: Causes 20-50% yield loss through defoliation; defoliated fruit suffers sunscald damage

classes.name: Tomato - Two-Spotted Spider Mite
symptoms: Tiny yellow or white stippling dots on upper leaf surface
Fine webbing on undersides of leaves and between leaves
Leaves turn bronze, yellow, or dry up and drop
Severe infestations cause complete defoliation
classes.causes: Caused by Tetranychus urticae mites; populations explode in hot, dry conditions; spreads by wind and human movement

treatment.chemical: Apply miticides (abamectin, bifenazate, spiromesifen); rotate chemical classes to prevent resistance
treatment.cultural: Spray plants with strong jets of water to dislodge mites, remove heavily infested leaves
treatment.preventive: Introduce predatory mites (Phytoseiidae), maintain adequate irrigation to reduce drought stress

classes.urgency: Medium-High - treat within 1 week; populations can double every 3-5 days in hot weather
classes.economic_impact: Can cause 30-50% yield reduction; market value drops significantly from damaged fruit

classes.name: Tomato - Target Spot
symptoms: Brown circular lesions with concentric ring pattern (target-like appearance)
Yellow halo surrounding lesions
Lesions appear on leaves, stems, and fruit
Fruit lesions are sunken and dark-centered
classes.causes: Caused by Corynespora cassiicola fungus; favored by warm temperatures and prolonged leaf wetness

treatment.chemical: Apply azoxystrobin, chlorothalonil, or copper-based fungicides at 7-14 day intervals
treatment.cultural: Improve air circulation by pruning and staking, avoid overhead irrigation, remove infected debris
treatment.preventive: Use resistant varieties, practice crop rotation, maintain good field sanitation

classes.urgency: Medium - treat within 1-2 weeks to prevent significant yield loss
classes.economic_impact: Can cause 20-30% yield loss; common in greenhouse and tropical production systems

classes.name: Tomato - Yellow Leaf Curl Virus
symptoms: Upward curling and cupping of young leaves
Yellowing (chlorosis) of leaf margins and veins
Severely stunted plant growth
Flower drop and near-complete fruit abortion in severe cases
classes.causes: Caused by Tomato yellow leaf curl virus (TYLCV); transmitted exclusively by silverleaf whitefly (Bemisia tabaci)

treatment.chemical: No cure for infected plants; control whitefly vectors with imidacloprid, acetamiprid, or insecticidal soaps
treatment.cultural: Remove and destroy infected plants immediately, use yellow sticky traps for whitefly monitoring
treatment.preventive: Plant resistant varieties (key strategy), use reflective mulches to repel whiteflies, use insect-proof netting in greenhouses

classes.urgency: High - no cure available; infected plants must be removed to protect remaining crop
classes.economic_impact: Can cause 70-100% yield loss if infection occurs early; major constraint to tomato production in tropical regions

classes.name: Tomato - Mosaic Virus
symptoms: Light and dark green mosaic mottling on leaves
Leaf malformation and curling
Stunted plant growth
Fruit may show yellow mottling or internal browning
classes.causes: Caused by Tomato mosaic virus (ToMV); transmitted mechanically through infected tools, hands, and plant contact

treatment.chemical: No chemical treatment available; focus on sanitation and vector control
treatment.cultural: Remove and destroy infected plants, disinfect tools with 10% bleach or 70% alcohol between plants, wash hands frequently
treatment.preventive: Plant virus-resistant varieties, use certified virus-free seeds, do not smoke near tomato plants (tobacco mosaic virus can infect tomatoes)

classes.urgency: Medium-High - no cure; remove infected plants to prevent spread via mechanical transmission
classes.economic_impact: Can cause 10-25% yield loss depending on infection timing; early infections cause more severe losses

classes.name: Tomato - Healthy
symptoms: Deep green, firm leaves with no lesions or discoloration
Normal leaf shape with no curling or mottling
Vigorous stem growth with no lesions
Normal fruit set and development
classes.causes: No disease present - plant is in excellent health

treatment.cultural: Continue regular pruning, staking, and monitoring
treatment.preventive: Maintain proper irrigation, scout weekly for early pest/disease detection, avoid excessive nitrogen

classes.urgency: None - plant is healthy, continue routine care
classes.economic_impact: No negative impact - healthy plants produce maximum yield and fruit quality

none.description: No disease detected - plant appears healthy

low.description: Minor infection - monitor closely and consider preventive treatment

moderate.description: Moderate infection - treatment recommended within 1-2 weeks

high.description: Severe infection - immediate treatment required to save crop

very_high.description: Critical infection - aggressive treatment needed, consider plant removal
